regime_context: Detector shows broad-but-shallow thematic leadership concentrated in Canadian materials/energy (Base Metals, Oil & Gas, Gold Miners all eligible and top-3), with no dominant one-narrative and weak cross-sectional momentum edge. The absolute-trend gate is validated for drawdown control on this market, so the state supports a vol-aware, trend-respecting posture rather than a predictive one. Track record shows hit_rate 66% but direction accuracy only 35% (below chance on raw 16-theme ranking), so all leans here default low conviction.
emerging_watch: Oil & Gas Producers (XEG.TO) is currently the challenger to Base Metals at rank 2, margin 0.11 — a lasting takeover of the rank-1 spot by Oil & Gas that holds for 10+ consecutive trading days would retire this watch; conversely the watch expires quietly if the margin re-widens to >0.3 in Base Metals' favor.

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Rank 1 with eligible=true and a positive trend-gate score (1.655) means the theme is both leading in cross-sectional focus AND passing the absolute-trend discipline — the one validated leg (drawdown/shake-out control) endorses staying power. Breadth 0.556 with ~56% of constituents participating and not crowded (z=0.9) means leadership is broadly distributed rather than a spiky one-name extension, so no immediate size-down pressure from crowding. Lean is a directional tilt toward the current leadership structure, not a claim that rank predicts returns (rank-IC ~0 per backtest).
evidence: rank=1, score=1.655, eligible=true (top of focus lens)
theses.dissent: Hurst tag mean-revert (0.5 durability bar, mid-range) and backtest verdict 'modest_or_none' on rank-IC mean this leadership is an attention concentration that can reverse without warning; copper/mining narratives are commodity-cycle-driven and this detector has no validated alpha at the theme level.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO gives back its trailing 30-day relative gain vs the S&P/TSX benchmark before check-by at day 30

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Rank 3, eligible=true, with breadth=0.4 and durability_bar=0.48 — lower participation than Base Metals but still passing the absolute-trend gate that is the only validated edge on this market. Crowding is absent (z=0.19) so no reflexive cap signal. Lean is modest because Gold Miners lags Oil & Gas in score and has mean-revert tag, but it remains one of only three eligible-and-unflagged top themes.
evidence: absolute_trend_gate validated on this market (staying-power leg)
theses.dissent: Breadth is only 0.4 and Hurst tag mean-revert signals the trend is not self-reinforcing; gold-miner moves are driven by FX/real-rate variables outside this detector's scope, so the lean is fragile to a macro shift.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms XBM.TO by more than 3% over the next 45 trading days

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Rank 5 with eligible=true but the lowest breadth among eligible themes (0.286) and a score of 0.7 well below the top commodities complex. The Hurst tag 'trend' suggests persistent direction, and the lean reflects that the trend-gate discipline (the validated leg) is not confirming broad participation — only ~29% of constituents are carrying the move, which is the opposite of the broad-based Base Metals structure. Underweight is a relative tilt within an eligible-but-thin theme, not a call that banks will fall.
evidence: breadth=0.286 — narrow participation vs Base Metals 0.556
hurst_tag=trend but durability_bar=0.6 — persistence without breadth
theses.dissent: Big Banks are the highest-earning, most liquid sector on the TSX and the 'trend' Hurst tag plus eligibility means the gate still endorses it; underweighting the only large-cap financials theme could hurt if commodities reverse and defensives rotate back.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO outperforms the S&P/TSX by 2% or more over the next 20 trading days

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
